findings.problem: status is a pub String, allowing any arbitrary string value including invalid workflow states
findings.failure_mode: callers can set item.status to "foo" or "" which represents an impossible workflow state, breaking all state-machine invariants
findings.fix: replace with an enum: pub enum WorkflowStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and make it private with a smart constructor

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are separate bool fields that can reach inconsistent combinations (e.g. is_sent=true but status not "sent", or is_validated=false but is_sent=true)
findings.failure_mode: no type-level enforcement of valid lifecycle transitions; callers can construct states like (validated=false, sent=true, status="pending") which is logically impossible
findings.fix: encode the lifecycle as an enum typestate (e.g. WorkflowState<T> with variants Pending, Validated(T), Sent { sent_at: u64 }) so invalid combinations are unrepresentable

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is an Option<u64> at the struct level rather than owned by the Sent variant
findings.failure_mode: is_sent can be true while sent_at_epoch_ms is None, or sent_at_epoch_ms can hold a value while is_sent is false; the timestamp is decoupled from the lifecycle phase that requires it
findings.fix: move sent_at_epoch_ms into the enum variant that represents the Sent phase: Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }

findings.problem: id is a bare pub String with no domain-level validation or newtype protection
findings.failure_mode: callers can create a SampleWorkflow with an empty, malformed, or unbounded id; no smart constructor enforces id constraints; String is not a domain-specific identifier
findings.fix: create a newtype: pub struct WorkflowId(String) or validate and wrap in a smart constructor returning Result<WorkflowId, ParseError>

findings.problem: raw String values for id and status cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct invalid domain states directly via public struct fields
findings.failure_mode: no boundary parsing means hostile or malformed input propagates into core logic as valid-looking data; every field is pub so there is no encapsulation gate
findings.fix: replace pub fields with a private struct and provide smart constructors like fn new(id: &str, initial_status: &str) -> Result<SampleWorkflow, ParseError> that validate and convert at the boundary

findings.problem: mark_sent blindly sets status and is_sent without validating preconditions (e.g. item must be validated first, status must be in a permissible pre-sent state)
findings.failure_mode: callers can call mark_sent on a workflow that was never validated, or on one already sent, violating lifecycle invariants with no runtime or compile-time check
findings.fix: change the function signature to accept the validated lifecycle phase explicitly (e.g. fn transition_to_sent(state: ValidatedWorkflow) -> SentWorkflow) so the type system enforces ordering

findings.problem: no benchmark, profiler, allocation, or command evidence exists for any performance or allocation claim in the crate
findings.failure_mode: any performance claim about mark_sent or SampleWorkflow is unmeasured folklore; Vec/String allocations and their costs are unknown
findings.fix: add a criterion or tinybench benchmark measuring mark_sent allocation profile with realistic input sizes

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent allocation or latency
no profiler evidence for hot-path analysis
no allocation audit (try_reserve, Vec::with_capacity, or bounded allocation evidence)
no verification gate commands run (cargo fmt/check/clippy/test)
residual_risk: The struct makes illegal states fully representable via pub String status, disjoint lifecycle booleans, and optional lifecycle data. mark_sent has no transition guards. All fixes require refactoring the type system (enum state machine + typestate transitions + smart constructors). Static review only; no commands executed.
